name: Console interjections, upgrade notices, group messaging skills

items.t: Fix: a message sent while the previous reply was still being delivered was refused with "wrapping up, please resend"
items.d: A message arriving at the moment a reply, card or the stop confirmation was still on its way to Feishu used to be refused. It now waits for that delivery and is handled in arrival order; a message sent right after /stop is answered normally.

items.t: New: the console can post a line into an idle group
items.d: A line written in the console is posted to the group as the administrator and handled as an ordinary group message, with the reply in the group. A busy, held or upgrading group is refused with the reason; resubmitting the same line is not processed twice.

items.t: New: a version notice card in each group after an upgrade
items.d: On the first start after an upgrade, each serving group receives one card listing what changed. Not sent on a first install or a downgrade; can be turned off in the console.

items.t: New: the agent in a group can send messages, notice cards and files, read history, reply, edit and recall
items.d: The agent gains group skills: send messages, notice cards, files and images, read the group history, reply to, edit and recall its own messages, download group files and add reactions.

name: /stop no longer pauses the group

items.t: Fix: /stop during a task could pause the whole group
items.d: /stop removes the task's reply card, and Feishu then reports that removal as a recall. When it arrived while "stopped" was still being sent, it was treated as a fault: the group was paused until an administrator released it, and later /model and /new were refused. The recall now waits for that reply to finish and the group keeps serving.

items.t: Fix: recalling a queued message could pause the group
items.d: Recalling a message while its "queued" notice was still being sent also paused the whole group; the message is now cancelled once the notice has been sent.

name: A rejected Codex resume no longer holds the group

items.t: Fix: a group held when Codex rejected a resume
items.d: When Codex refused to continue the previous conversation before doing any work (for example a damaged Codex session history on the machine, or a conversation whose record is gone), the whole group was paused until an administrator released it. Now the group gets one "the last turn did not finish, please send it again" notice, keeps serving, and starts a new conversation, so resending works.

items.t: Fix: a queued message stalled the group after a start failure
items.d: When the model could not start (program missing or resume rejected), messages queued behind it each get a resend notice; before, the next new message was treated as a busy group and the whole group was paused.

name: Group commands, console settings and Codex sign-in

items.t: New /skip in groups
items.d: Drops only the current task; queued messages run next and the conversation is kept. /stop still cancels the current task and everything queued.

items.t: /help is written for each group
items.d: It opens with the group's project and model, lists commands by urgency, describes /skip, /stop and /new in the same terms (what happens to the queue and to the conversation), and explains that recalling your own message cancels it.

items.t: New session from the console
items.d: An idle group with every record settled starts a new conversation right away; a busy group is told to stop or wait first instead of being reported as reset.

items.t: Models can be added and configured from the model cards
items.d: No service restart. Changing a model id, backend or endpoint waits for the groups using it to be idle and starts a new conversation for them; the default model and models in use cannot be hidden.

items.t: Fix: tool quality and thinking depth settings could not be saved
items.d: They were wrongly reported as needing a service restart.

items.t: Codex sign-in is checked with the server
items.d: The console's Codex model card no longer trusts the local sign-in file alone. It asks the server once with the token and shows one of three states: verified, sign-in expired (run codex login again on this machine), or unverified (the server could not be reached; not treated as signed out). A revoked token no longer keeps showing as signed in.

items.t: Fix: stopping a task before it started could swallow the next answer
items.d: If the model process failed to start after a console stop or /skip, a stale cancelled flag could silently drop the next task's answer.

name: Upgrade progress in the console

items.t: Confirm the upgrade in the page
items.d: Upgrade now asks for confirmation in the page, stating the versions and that new messages wait about a minute during the switch.

items.t: The upgrade window shows each step
items.d: Waiting for idle groups, download and install, stopping the current service, checking records and backing up, preflight, switching and starting, and waiting for every group to connect are ticked off one by one with the elapsed time; while waiting it names the groups still working.

items.t: Reconnects while the service restarts
items.d: During the switch the page says the service is restarting and reconnects by itself; once the new version connects every group it reloads into the new console and shows the result once. A failed step and the restored version are marked.

items.t: Can run in the background
items.d: Continue in background keeps a spinner on the top-bar icon, which reopens the progress; a notice appears when the upgrade ends.

items.t: Takes effect from 1.4.4
items.d: The upgrade window comes from the running version: upgrading from 1.4.3 to 1.4.4 still shows the previous screen, and later upgrades show the window.

name: Progress on the reply card

items.t: A card appears even before any output
items.d: If nothing has been produced after 25 seconds, a "Received, working on it" card appears and the answer later replaces it in place. A turn that ends without a reply recalls that card.

items.t: The card shows how far the task has got
items.d: While running, one line updates every 15 seconds: how long it has run and what it is doing (reading, editing or writing which file, running a command, searching the web; file names only). After 10 minutes it updates once a minute, and notes when nothing has happened for more than 2 minutes. Delivered steps such as writing files, committing or pushing, and sending files to the group are listed with ▶ at the top of the card and fold into a "Process" section when the turn ends.

items.t: /status shows progress
items.d: While running it shows how many steps have run, how long ago the last activity was, and what it is doing.

items.t: Fix: a streamed reply could fail the whole turn
items.d: Text that arrived while the previous update was still being sent used to fail the turn; it now queues behind it and keeps updating the card.

name: Check and install new versions from the console

items.t: Version checks in the console
items.d: Software updates in Settings checks for stable releases at startup and daily and shows release notes when a new version is available.

items.t: One-click upgrade for background runs
items.d: When a launchd agent runs SintBot, Upgrade now waits until every group is idle and settled, installs the new version into its own folder and switches to it; if it does not connect every group within 90 seconds, the previous version is restored. New messages wait about a minute during the switch and are asked to be resent.

items.t: Steps for foreground runs
items.d: A foreground run shows how to stop, reinstall and start. Upgrades are not announced in groups.

name: A failing group stops only itself

items.t: One group's fault leaves the others working
items.d: When a group's last task has an outcome that cannot be confirmed (for example a reply whose delivery is unknown, or a runner that exited without a result), only that group is paused; nothing is replayed or retried and the other groups keep working. A paused group answers new messages with a short notice.

items.t: One group no longer blocks startup
items.d: If a group's records cannot be recovered, the other groups still start and the console marks that group Needs attention. The startup preflight fails and lists such groups.

items.t: Incident seal command
items.d: Restart first; for a group that is still paused, stop the service and run sintbot incident seal --group <group ID>. The old records are kept unchanged, the group reopens with new records, and messages left unfinished before the seal are not processed again.

name: Multiple groups, Claude Code and chat commands

items.t: One app serves several groups
items.d: One Feishu app can bind 1–32 groups, each to a local project with its own records; a concurrency limit caps simultaneous tasks.

items.t: Codex or Claude Code per group
items.d: Each group chooses its runner and model. Send /model to list or switch; a switch happens only while that group is idle and starts a new conversation.

items.t: Chat commands
items.d: Adds /help, /status, /new, /hud and /issue for status, quota and usage, a new conversation and feedback. An unsupported command gets a one-line notice and never stops the service.

items.t: Reply cards update while working
items.d: The card appears once the model starts answering and refreshes with progress.

items.t: Local console
items.d: Start with --ui to see every group, stop tasks, bind new groups, switch the model or project of an idle group, and handle feedback.

items.t: A failure stays in its group
items.d: When a turn returns a model error or no result, only that group is asked to resend, with no automatic retry; other groups keep working. Groups added to the configuration are registered at restart.

name: Built-in core

items.t: Adds a built-in core
items.d: This release supports Codex messages in one Feishu group on macOS. Whiteboards, multiple groups and other platforms will follow. Keep existing multi-group installations and configure this release separately using the installation guide.

name: Follow-up notice fix

items.t: No false queue notice right after a task starts
items.d: A follow-up sent in the first few seconds joins the running task once the channel is ready, without first saying it will wait until the task ends.

name: Steadier follow-ups, clearer errors

items.t: The reply card follows the latest follow-up
items.d: Once a follow-up is accepted, the card moves under that message, so the answer ends up at the bottom of the group. A short notice is sent only when the card cannot move.

items.t: Recalls and redos no longer lose messages
items.d: A recalled follow-up that had not been delivered no longer runs on its own. A redo in a new session or on another model keeps delivered follow-ups, except recalled ones.

items.t: Codex requests no longer stall a task
items.d: Approval and question requests are declined according to the protocol, and the task continues.

items.t: Console messages can join the running task
items.d: A console message with Reply checked is treated like a group member's. The group line is posted first, the dialog says where the message will go, and the result reports where it landed.

items.t: Feishu answer cards show the model and quota
items.d: The small print on the card now includes the current model and account quota.

items.t: Plain explanations for network and billing errors
items.d: Network failures, low balance and expired subscriptions are explained in the group. Repeated network failures alert the operator, and account problems can fail over.

items.t: Lost sessions are redone automatically
items.d: Claude and Codex groups clear a session that no longer exists, redo the message in a new one, and say so in the group.

name: Codex busy follow-up

items.t: Codex can receive follow-ups during a task
items.d: Busy follow-up is on by default for Codex groups. Ordinary human follow-up messages enter the active task through the App Server; related requests can adjust the work, independent requests are answered separately in order, and unconfirmed deliveries return to the queue. It can be disabled per group; Claude groups and scheduled, quiet, and polled messages keep their existing behavior.

items.t: Busy follow-up is limited to the effective Codex backend
items.d: The console shows the control for the backend currently in use, and the server validates it too. Changes apply from the next turn.

name: More reliable installs and runs

items.t: Installs are verified by running the program
items.d: After installing a model CLI, setup runs it once to confirm its version. A file on disk or a clean installer exit no longer counts as success, and a failed check explains what went wrong and what to do next.

items.t: Health checks ignore files that cannot run
items.d: Files without execute permission are no longer reported as installed programs. Automatic installs also keep the platform components the CLI needs to run.

items.t: Finds a model CLI that has moved
items.d: If the configured path stops working, SintBot looks for the same program in common install locations and keeps going. If it is nowhere to be found, the group gets a plain explanation and the operator gets an alert.

items.t: Clearer handling of lost logins and crashes
items.d: A revoked login token now counts as an account problem, so the group can fail over and alert. A Codex run that exits with only an error gets the same treatment.

items.t: Fixed occasional garbled Chinese
items.d: Characters split across output chunks no longer turn into garbage.

name: Safer AI-assisted setup, quieter design tools

items.t: Safer AI-assisted installation
items.d: API keys are masked as they are entered in the local terminal, keeping them out of AI conversation logs. Without an interactive terminal, the installer stops if Node is missing or too old; otherwise it skips model setup and the background service and explains what remains.

items.t: Clearer install and first-use flow
items.d: Add bilingual guides for AI-assisted installation and first use. The one-line preview lists planned operations and confirmations, and warns that a model trial may use quota or incur a charge.

items.t: Design and icon libraries on demand
items.d: Both libraries are collapsed by default; style presets are recommended only for a new product with no visual direction yet.

name: Clearer console settings

items.t: Software updates and history together
items.d: Update controls and version history now share one card at the bottom of Settings. A small dot appears by the version number when a newer stable release is available.

items.t: A wider Bot & network card
items.d: The card spans the full settings grid, with the bot name and proxy arranged side by side. Background proxy details can be expanded when needed.

name: Steadier service installs and better console controls

items.t: More reliable service reinstalls
items.d: A reinstall now waits for the old background service to fully unload before starting the new one, reducing cases where the service is left unloaded.

items.t: Software updates from the console
items.d: Stable releases are checked at startup and daily, with a manual check available too. An administrator confirms an upgrade, which waits for every group task and queue to clear before installing the exact version.

items.t: Manage console access in Settings
items.d: Set a password for LAN access and toggle LAN binding or public Feishu sign-in. Turning off public sign-in revokes existing Feishu sessions; a failed binding change restores the previous settings.

name: An even shorter install: almost nothing to answer

items.t: No questions for what can be done automatically
items.d: The one-line install upgrades to the latest version directly. The wizard installs Claude Code when it is missing, picks the default model itself and runs a trial turn, and no longer asks about adding more models; Codex and the design icon libraries are optional and only get a one-line install hint. If you are already logged in to Claude or Codex, the whole install asks one thing: whether to install the background service.

items.t: Keys and proxy go into the service automatically
items.d: Installing the background service writes the environment-variable keys the config refers to, and your terminal's proxy, into the service definition (mode 600) without asking. Run sintbot service install again after changing a key or the proxy.

items.t: Less output
items.d: The install no longer shows npm progress or harmless warnings, and the background service reports a single line when it is up.

name: Simpler install: the terminal sets up the model, the console does the rest

items.t: The terminal only sets up the model
items.d: The setup wizard no longer asks whether the machine is in mainland China, or for a proxy, a projects folder or chat platform credentials. In the terminal it checks the environment and sets up a model with a live trial turn; everything else is set in the console afterwards. The old full set of questions is still available as sintbot setup --full, for servers without a browser.

items.t: A console right after install
items.d: The background service now installs even before a chat platform is connected: it runs the console only (http://127.0.0.1:4600), and the one-line install opens it in your browser. Connect a platform under Settings and save; the service restarts itself within seconds and connects. The Overview page has a new Get started checklist.

items.t: Bot name and network proxy in the console
items.d: Settings → Bot & network sets how the bot refers to itself and the network proxy. Service install can also carry your terminal's proxy into the service.

items.t: English throughout, and small fixes
items.d: The installer and the wizard speak Chinese or English following the system language (on macOS, the system language). The site a Zhipu or MiniMax key belongs to is found automatically. An up-to-date install is no longer reinstalled, and sintbot ui opens the running service's console. Fixed wizard questions being overwritten by "> " and a stray *.0.1 in the direct-connection list.

name: Icon libraries from the setup wizard

items.t: The wizard installs the icon libraries
items.d: When the design icon libraries (Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor and Pixelarticons) are missing, the setup wizard now offers to install them in one go (about 170 MB). With them, the bot uses standard icons by name when it draws a design instead of drawing its own.

name: A steadier background service

items.t: No service without a chat platform
items.d: If no Feishu, Slack or WeCom bot is connected yet, installing the background service now stops and points you to the console to connect one and bind a group first. Before, the service would exit as soon as it started.

items.t: Keys from environment variables reach the service
items.d: When the config takes keys from environment variables, installing the service now asks whether to write them into the service definition, readable only by you. Without them, models that use those keys do not work in the service.

items.t: Clearer wording
items.d: Trial runs show the model from your config instead of the model's own claim (third-party models often call themselves Claude). The health check gives a missing chat platform a row of its own, and in a local terminal trial the model-switch hint says how to switch.

name: A steadier setup wizard

items.t: No more looping without a terminal
items.d: When the setup wizard runs without keyboard input (in a script, a container or CI), it now finishes on the defaults instead of looping at the model step until the disk fills, and it no longer installs Claude Code on its own. If it still cannot finish, it stops and writes no config.

name: A clearer console, sharper style extraction

items.t: "Needs you" on the console
items.d: The top of Overview lists what is waiting on you: failed tasks with their reason, browser takeovers nobody has claimed, open feedback, leftover background processes and failing health checks. It appears only when something does, and sends nothing extra to any group.

items.t: Activity survives restarts
items.d: After a restart or an upgrade, live activity on Overview is filled back in from recent tasks, and failed tasks show their reason.

items.t: Sharper style extraction
items.d: Extracting from a URL now reads stylesheets a site serves from other domains, so sites like Feishu and Bilibili work, and sites that need a proxy go through the configured one. Colors, fonts and radii are read more accurately, and anything it cannot read leaves your choices as they were.

items.t: English throughout
items.d: The English console now covers the WeCom settings, health checks, scheduled-task descriptions and more, and the built-in design styles have English names and descriptions.

name: First official release

items.t: One group, one project
items.d: Bind a Feishu, Slack or WeCom group to a project and anyone in the group can hand it work; each group has its own session, queue and permissions.

items.t: Switch models anytime
items.d: Claude, GPT (through Codex), DeepSeek, GLM, MiniMax or a custom endpoint — each group picks its own and can switch at any time without losing the project memory.

items.t: Progress in the group
items.d: Work in progress streams to a progress card in the group, and the result is posted back when it is done.

items.t: Local console
items.d: Manage groups, models and chat platforms in the browser, run a test turn and read the version history; it can also be opened to your LAN or reached through a public entry.

items.t: Easy to start
items.d: One-line install; the setup wizard recommends a model based on the accounts you already have and tries it on the spot, and the health check reports honestly what works and what needs fixing.

items.t: Your data stays on your machine
items.d: Projects, sessions and memory stay on your own machine, and messages sent to the group are redacted automatically.
